sources.entry: Build a Todo List App in JavaScript

summary.one_liner: A step-by-step tutorial for building a Todo List app in vanilla JavaScript using TDD with Tape and JSDOM and a small Elm-style micro framework called elmish.
summary.what_it_does: The README walks through building a TodoMVC-styled todo list app from scratch in plain JavaScript, without a UI framework. It follows The Elm Architecture pattern with a model object, an update function driven by a switch on action names, and view functions that render DOM elements. Each feature (adding items, toggling done state, rendering the list, footer with item count and filter links, and the overall view) is introduced as a test first and then implemented. The tutorial relies on a helper library called elmish (documented in elmish.md) that supplies DOM helpers such as mount, div, input, and route. The README also covers storing todos in localStorage and routing filters via the URL hash. Only a truncated portion of the README was provided, so later sections may cover additional details.
use_cases: learn vanilla JavaScript by building a todo app
learn The Elm Architecture pattern in plain JavaScript
practice test-driven development with Tape and JSDOM
study a TodoMVC-style app without a framework
understand how a tiny front-end framework is built
how_to_run: git clone the repository (URL truncated in README)
notable: Test-driven tutorial: each feature begins with a failing Tape test before implementation
Uses a homemade Elm-inspired micro framework (elmish) with mount, div, input, route helpers
Computes item counts at render time rather than storing them in the model
Persists todos to localStorage so they survive page refresh
Reuses the TodoMVC CSS so the focus stays on functionality
caveats: README is truncated, so the full set of sections and final code were not visible
Explicitly educational: elmish is described as meant only for educational purposes, not production use
Requires Node.js and npm for the test setup, and a browser to view the final app
keywords: make a to-do list in javascript
